# nosms — full manual (llms-full.txt)

This is the expandable companion to `llms.txt`. `llms.txt` is the contract; this
file is the manual. Both are served by the CVM server (`docs` and `llms-full`
tools, and as the resources `nosms://llms.txt` / `nosms://llms-full.txt`) and
committed here so a human or an agent can read them without a relay.

## 1. What the service is

nosms sends one SMS to one phone number on behalf of a nostr key. There is no
account, no API key and no signup: your nostr key is identity and you pay per
message in sats, postage-style. The v1 rail is a single personal JMP/Cheogram
line sold as a risk-priced service (ADR-0002), so treat volume limits as real.

## 2. Two surfaces, one transport contract

| Surface | Who uses it | How |
|---|---|---|
| ContextVM (MCP over Nostr, kind `25910`) | agents, in-shell clients | call the tools by server npub |
| HTTP (`https://nosms.orangesync.tech`) | scripts, `curl`, LLMs with network access | NIP-98-authenticated `POST /api/send` |

Both sit on the same `Transport` interface and the same price table, so a price
or capability change cannot be visible on one surface and stale on the other.

A napplet cannot use the HTTP surface: `NAP-RESOURCE` is bytes-in/bytes-out with
no HTTP verb, so a `POST` with a body is not expressible from a sandboxed
napplet. That is exactly why the napplet wraps the CVM.

## 3. Tools

### `sms.send(to, body, cashu_token?, settlement_receipt?)` — PAID

- `to` — E.164 destination (`+14155550100`). Formatting is stripped; a value with
  no digits, or too short to be a phone number, is `bad_destination`.
- `body` — the message text (non-empty).
- `cashu_token` — the ecash, in `cashuA…` (v3) or `cashuB…` (v4) encoding. The
  service decodes it, checks the mint, checks NUT-07 proof states, charges the
  NUT-02 input fee **to the sender**, and captures the value with a NUT-03 swap.
- `settlement_receipt` — the shell's CEP-8 settlement receipt, for callers whose
  shell already escrowed. Honoured only where the service has no mint to re-swap
  against; otherwise pass `cashu_token`.

Result fields:

- `id` — the send record id, used with `sms.status`.
- `to` — the normalised E.164 destination.
- `price_sats` — what postage was taken (0 for the owner).
- `accepted` — `true` when the rail accepted the message for dispatch.
- `rail` — the rail name that accepted it.
- `best_effort` — echoed from the rail's own capability flags.
- `delivery_confirmed` — always `false` on a `best_effort` rail. Never a claim.
- `refunded` / `refund_token` — set when a hard failure was refunded.
- `status` — the rail's accept-time status (`queued`/`sent`/`delivered`/`failed`).

### `sms.status(id)` — free

Returns the stored send record: destination, price paid, rail, acceptance and
any refund. It never claims delivery on a rail that cannot observe it.

### `sms.pricing(to?)` — free

Live price in sats. Returns `unit`, `model: "flat"`, the flat `price`, the raw
`quote_sats` from the ADR-0002 formula with the `btc_usd` used, the `mult` and
`rail_replacement_usd` inputs, the `floor_sats`, and — when `to` is given — the
normalised destination and its price. An invalid destination is refused.

### `sms.capabilities` — free

The rail name and its capability flags, read from the rail itself:

- `best_effort` — `true` means there is no retry guarantee.
- `delivery_receipts` — `false` means NO delivery confirmation is possible.
- `countries` — destinations the rail will attempt.

### `docs` (alias `llms`) — free

Returns the `llms.txt` contract verbatim. Callers must not need out-of-band
knowledge: everything required to use the service is reachable from the server.

### `llms-full` — free

Returns this manual.

## 4. Payment (CEP-8)

- Gating: `explicit_gating`. An unpaid `sms.send` is answered with a visible
  `payment_required` error carrying the `cap`, `pmi` and `gating` fields — never
  silence.
- Capability tags: `cap:tool:sms.send:2900:sats` (flat, ADR-0002).
- PMI: `bitcoin-cashu` (primary). A Lightning PMI may be added later.
- Refunds: a hard failure the rail can detect is refunded automatically. A
  `best_effort` miss — the rail accepted and the carrier silently dropped the
  message — is NOT refundable, because the rail cannot see it.
- Owner allowlist: the operator's own npub sends free. Every other caller pays.

## 5. Error contract

Every refusal is a JSON-RPC `result` with `isError: true` and a body carrying a
machine `reason` and a human `hint`. Reasons: `payment_required`,
`insufficient_funds`, `bad_destination`, `destination_unsupported`,
`rail_not_configured`, `transport_error`, `rail_unavailable`, `rail_paced`,
`rate_limited`, `owner_only`,
`token_invalid`, `token_wrong_mint`, `token_already_spent`, `token_state_unknown`,
`mint_error`, `mint_unreachable`, `not_found`, `unsupported method`.

The HTTP surface carries the same vocabulary as `X-Reason` / `X-Hint` headers.

## 6. Honest limits (read before building on this)

1. **No delivery receipts.** `sms.send` returning `accepted: true` means the rail
   took the message. It does not mean the handset received it. Do not build OTP
   confirmation, escrow release on delivery, or any delivery-dependent logic.
2. **Best effort.** No retry guarantee.
3. **One personal line.** Throughput is that of a single phone number.
4. **Countries.** The rail reports what it will attempt (`[US, CA]`); it does not
   guarantee coverage.
5. **Termination risk.** The rail is a personal consumer line used as a paid
   service against its operator's automation policy. It can be terminated at any
   time; pricing and the degrade path to the email rail are the mitigations.

## 7. Data handling

Destination numbers and message bodies are retained only for status lookups and
refunds. No marketing use, no third-party sharing, no analytics. Message bodies
on the HTTP surface are NIP-44-encrypted client-to-gateway and are never stored
in plaintext at the service.

## 8. Running the server

```
python3 scripts/run_cvm_server.py --relays wss://relay.contextvm.org \
    wss://relay2.contextvm.org wss://relay.primal.net --announce
python3 scripts/run_cvm_server.py            # then listen
```

The client and the server MUST use different nostr keys: a shared key makes the
client receive its own gift-wrapped requests and the response correlation breaks.

---
*Manual version: v2 (2026-10-05). The authoritative values are always the live
`sms.pricing` and `sms.capabilities` responses.*
